A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including distinguishing retained material from additions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic simulations, DisLib experiments and ImageNet-X representation analyses in Section 4, plus a supplementary synthetic ablation in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulations and benchmark experiments, revises the ImageNet-X analysis and adds synthetic sensitivity and label-noise experiments in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The DIET encoder, linear classification head, instance-discrimination objective and supervised cross-entropy procedure are retained. The added assumptions, experimental variants and implementation disclosures do not introduce a new learning procedure.

E1.justification: The synthetic recovery task, DisLib datasets and ImageNet-X are retained. Appendix D extends synthetic scenarios to generalized-normal and truncated-Laplace conditionals and corrupted instance/class labels, providing a limited expansion within the existing synthetic domain.

E2.justification: The ImageNet-X comparison substantially broadens its controls. v1 compares trained ResNet50 and ViT-B/16 representations against shuffled labels; v3 adds projected-input and randomly initialized ResNet50/ViT-B/16 decoding baselines, with a 50% chance reference. The DisLib comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: ImageNet-X changes from accuracy, correlation and F1 reporting on imbalanced labels to accuracy after balancing both training and testing samples. New synthetic protocols examine batch-size/concentration and cluster-count/dimensionality combinations, distribution truncation and probabilistic label corruption.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained centroid-distribution ablation in Table 5, Figures 4–6 investigate conditional-distribution misspecification, heavy tails, batch-size effects, cluster diversity and label-noise robustness. These substantially expand the evidence about recovery failures and robustness.

E5.justification: v1 displays one shuffled-label comparison for ImageNet-X without corresponding uncertainty intervals or significance tests. v3 reports SEM across 10 balanced-resampling seeds and one-sample t-tests against 50% accuracy with Bonferroni adjustment at 0.05/85. Existing five-seed synthetic and three-seed DisLib reporting is retained.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 2–5 are unchanged. Figure 3 replaces the ImageNet-X results under a different evaluation protocol and adds control scores, so these are not same-setting performance gains. Figures 4–6 add substantial results, including limited recovery degradation through 80% label noise followed by sharp deterioration at 100%.

T1.justification: v1 states the supervised-identifiability theorem but leaves Appendix A.3 empty. v3 introduces Assumption 3 requiring uniformly distributed semantic classes, updates the main theorem to invoke it, and supplies a detailed supervised derivation in Appendix A.3. The existing DIET proof is largely retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion explicitly qualify latent recovery as holding under a particular cluster-centric DGP. This limits the presentation of the guarantee while retaining the central contributions concerning DIET, supervised classification and their connection to nonlinear ICA.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 explicitly excludes imbalanced semantic classes from the supervised guarantee. Appendix D adds mechanism hypotheses involving loss saturation, finite-batch gradients, cluster diversity, heavy tails and symmetric label noise. Section 4.3 also adds interpretations involving representation size and shape information; the existing proxy-latent caveat is retained and relocated.

D1.justification: v3 adds code-access information and an experimental-details appendix. Newly documented details include DisLib provenance, Adam training for 100 epochs at learning rate 0.001 and batch size 4096, plus ImageNet-X's 70/30 split, logistic-regression decoder and input projection. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: v3 acknowledges supervised and multitask identifiability work by Ahuja, Lachapelle and Fumero, qualifying its positioning. Additional references support discussions of label noise, dimensional collapse, shape bias and dataset provenance. The central positioning through ICA, DIET and supervised classification remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained, with targeted wording edits, standardized concentration notation, updated cross-references and author/header changes. Experimental details receive a separate Appendix C, while the previous supplementary-results appendix becomes Appendix D.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes from six scatterplots to grouped accuracy panels with error bars and significance markers. Figures 4–6 add heatmaps and line plots. Existing figures, tables and captions are repositioned, and the main text is substantially reflowed, including text wrapping around tables.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps by supplying the previously missing supervised derivation and making its uniform-class restriction explicit. The revised ImageNet-X study addresses imbalance and adds informative controls and uncertainty reporting; the new appendix analyses probe failure conditions, and implementation disclosures improve reproducibility. Dropping correlation/F1 reduces metric breadth, but the better controlled evidence and clearer theoretical scope provide a substantial net improvement.
